stories.completionNotes: US-504 CARVED into US-504a (writer) + this (producer) on the story's own conditionalOutcome -- it grew, and the writer half turned out to be a different, larger animal (see US-504a + the PM note). Every Spool [EXACT] value implemented verbatim, none drifted: 600 gate / 727 baseline / 80-60 bands / 180-day window / 90-day staleness / median-of-3. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: AC2 called the writer-fix a BLOCKING sub-story on the grounds that 'without this the verdict has nothing to consume' -- that premise is wrong. Spool's own verdict spec reads start_timestamp/end_timestamp/runtime_seconds/load_class and never touches vcell or soc, so the producer was fully buildable without it and is now built + green. That is why this half landed first rather than stalling behind a story that needs two rulings. THE SPEC BUG WORTH THE MOST ATTENTION (filed to Spool 2026-08-02): the qualifying gate (runtime_seconds >= 600) sits entirely ABOVE both sub-good bands (degraded 436-582s, replace <436s). Every row that survives the gate is >=600s therefore >=582s therefore always 'good' -- so through the real pipeline degraded and replace are UNREACHABLE, and a pack that genuinely dies at 500s is filtered out as a 'partial drain' rather than reported as degraded. The verdict silently cannot degrade; it fails safe toward reassurance, the wrong direction for an honest instrument. Implemented VERBATIM anyway (both numbers are [EXACT] Spool values -- flag, never drift), with the bands isolated in a public verdictForMedianRuntime() so the mapping stays fully exercised by tests and only the gate constant has to move when he rules. SECOND CORRECTION for the record: AC2's 'nothing populates start_vcell_v/end_vcell_v/start_soc_pct/end_soc_pct' is right at the data and wrong at the mechanism -- the recorder writes all four correctly and the bench CLI uses them; there is simply ZERO production caller in src/ since US-442/TD-058 retired the auto-open path. So no running Pi writes ANY row, and the card reads 'unknown' permanently rather than 'until fresh drains exist'. That is US-504a. HONEST-INSTRUMENT throughout: unknown is the DEFAULT, never a swallowed failure -- absent DB, unreadable log, unparseable clock, <3 qualifying rows in the trailing 180 days, or a >90-day-stale last check all resolve to unknown, and the staleness override is checked BEFORE the numbers so a stale reading can never paint a confident verdict of any colour. Today that override fires (newest qualifying row 2026-05-16, 78 days) -- the card correctly reads unknown + 2026-05-16, which is the instrument working. ONE VOCABULARY END-TO-END: the old green/attn/low display tiers were a SECOND enum for the same fact (the cross-module enum-identity class that cost the 9-drain saga) and are RETIRED -- battery_health_emitter now re-exports the producer's good/degraded/replace/unknown rather than declaring its own, and carousel.js healthLevel/healthValue speak those words. Severity per Spool: good->ok, degraded AND replace->neutral, unrecognised->unavailable. 'replace' is deliberately NOT red (the UPS carries ~12min against the <1min a clean shutdown needs -- a thinned data-integrity margin is not a car risk) and deliberately NOT ok either (that would claim health the data does not support); neutral is the only tier that neither alarms nor reassures. TEMP tile REMOVED -- the MAX17048 register map has no temperature at all, so the tile rendered 'not captured' on every row ever logged; the ambient_temp_c COLUMN stays for the BMP390. Verdict read is LAZY per emit via getattr, not captured at emitter construction -- the boot-order trap this sprint has now hit in US-501, US-502 and here; it also means a drain recorded while the orchestrator runs reaches the card without a restart. B-104 is respected rather than worked around: the producer reads identity + start wall-time ONLY and computes no distance/duration/max/avg, because derived per-drive analytics became the SERVER's authority when US-351 retired the Pi-side drive_statistics table -- re-deriving them here would rebuild exactly what that story deleted. THE ROOT, corrected: the tile did not read 'No recent drive' because a drive was missing, it read it PERMANENTLY. The card had only drive.driveId to read, which is the ACTIVE drive and is null whenever nothing is recording; no producer for the most-recent-COMPLETED drive existed anywhere. The absence was real -- it was the absence of a producer, which is why this could never have self-corrected after a drive. THE DESIGN CALL WORTH KNOWING: the anchor is drive START, not drive end. drive_summary has NO end-of-drive column -- there is no Pi-local record of when a drive finished. Synthesising one (e.g. the newest realtime_data sample) would be a guess dressed as a measurement, and doubly so while capture is down (BL-025), so the fact carried is the one that actually exists. Age is likewise formatted at DISPLAY time from the carried timestamp, never pre-computed at emit: a baked '2 h ago' freezes and ages visibly wrong on a kiosk that emits every few seconds but is read minutes later (same pattern the battery card already uses with lastHealthCheckTs). SIM ROWS ARE FILTERED, not relabelled -- presenting a physics_sim bench run as 'your last drive' would be a fabrication in the only terms the panel has. Consequence to know: on a simulator-only box the tile correctly reads 'No recent drive', which can LOOK like a regression; it is logged at debug distinguishably from 'no rows at all' for exactly that reason. ONE VOCABULARY: agoText extends the EXISTING ageText downward (just now / N min / N h) and hands back to it at a day, so '1 day ago' has exactly one definition on the whole surface -- a second age enum for the same fact is the cross-module enum-identity drift that cost the 9-drain saga. HONEST-INSTRUMENT, per HALF: a drive whose start timestamp is missing/blank/unparseable still renders the drive and admits 'age unknown', because the drive genuinely happened and hiding it would lose a real fact to protect a cosmetic one; a FUTURE stamp reads 'just now' rather than a negative age (the Pi has no RTC battery and boots before NTP settles, so a stamp ahead of now is a routine transient); absent DB, missing table, locked file, empty table or a non-integer drive id all resolve to the honest unknown. lastDrive is ALWAYS a key (null when unknown), never sometimes-absent -- an intermittently-missing key is the shape that lets a renderer quietly fall through to the wrong branch. Boot-order trap avoided for the FOURTH time this sprint (US-501/502/504b were the others): the database is resolved via getattr AT USE TIME, so a drive recorded while the orchestrator runs reaches the card without a service restart. stories.completionNotes: ROOT, stated precisely because the AC's phrasing understates it: an rfcomm bind is a KERNEL TABLE ENTRY, and it outlives the ACL link. When the dongle drops, /dev/rfcomm0 and the bind record are both still there -- so bindRfcomm's IDEMPOTENT short-circuit ('already bound to the right MAC') hands the retry the same DEAD tty, forever. That is the stale-rfcomm-retry-forever signature. THE ONE THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: the entry also outlives the PROCESS. A SIGKILLed/crashed predecessor never ran disconnect(), so its binding is still in the kernel table at startup; the new ObdConnection has _boundRfcomm=False, its disconnect (which releases only a binding IT created) skips, bindRfcomm short-circuits on the inherited entry, and the fresh process opens the predecessor's dead tty. So `systemctl restart` did NOT clear this fault -- which is exactly why it read as unfixable in the field. The release therefore had to be keyed on 'the configured port is a MAC', NOT on our own bookkeeping. Pinned by test_connect_staleBindingInheritedFromAPriorProcess_isDroppedNotReused. SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE TRACING (not in the AC, and it made the first one unrecoverable): bt_resilience._reactToAdapterUnreachable called _safeDisconnect() -- which RELEASES the binding -- and then waited on ReconnectLoop, whose probe is isRfcommReachable, which REQUIRES the binding to exist. The recovery was waiting for a state its own teardown had just removed, so waitForAdapter could never report success and the reopen never ran. That is why Spool's path ends in a RE-BIND rather than a release: resetTransport() leaves the transport freshly BOUND, which is what makes the probe answer honestly again. AC1 is therefore satisfied at THREE call sites, not one: (a) ObdConnection.reconnect() -> resetTransport(); (b) the per-failed-attempt binding drop inside _performConnect -- the ONLY reset the US-338 post-failure heartbeat ever gets, since it drives connect() and never touches reconnect(); (c) the mixin's ADAPTER_UNREACHABLE path. Missing (b) would have left the heartbeat -- the path that actually runs for hours in the car -- entirely unfixed while every reconnect() test stayed green. AC2 (durable bond): the pair-time half was already shipped (the 2026-07-31 P0 hotfix writes + VERIFIES Paired+Bonded+Trusted). What did not exist was the RUNTIME half -- nothing ever read those flags back. A bond that loses Trusted still reports as paired, but bluez refuses the unattended reconnect, so the symptom is a mystery dead link whose only apparent remedy is a manual re-pair -- which needs the dongle powered, i.e. the engine running, i.e. exactly when you cannot do it. ensureTrusted() repairs trust (a local bluez flag, repairable unattended) and reports an absent bond record honestly with the actual remedy, rather than issuing a trust that cannot help. Best-effort by construction: it can never fail a connect that would otherwise have worked. AC4: no rfkill / hciconfig / nmcli / `power off` anywhere on any new path -- guarded at BOTH the helper level and across the whole recovery, because systemd-rfkill persists radio state at shutdown and that is precisely how the 07-03 soft-block became sticky. eclipse-rfkill-unblock.service stays the standing net; this avoids needing it. stories.goal: As the maintainer, I want to know WHY the BT rfkill soft-block got saved ~07-03, so we can prevent the origin, not just rely on the unblock safety net.
stories.completionNotes: RCA VERDICT: origin UNPROVABLE at this remove; project EXONERATED; mitigation found INSUFFICIENT and hardened. Taking those in order. (1) ORIGIN -- I did NOT name a culprit, deliberately. All three forensic sources are destroyed or out of range: the saved-state file was OVERWRITTEN by the 07-31 recovery (mtime now 2026-07-31 20:26:02, contents 0, and `sudo rm -f /var/lib/systemd/rfkill/*` appears in the Pi's bash_history), the systemd journal retains only back to 2026-07-26 12:39:54 (07-03 is ~3 weeks outside the window), and ~/.bash_history covers only the 07-31 recovery session -- and would never have caught an agent's commands anyway, since `ssh host "cmd"` is non-interactive and does not append to history. Naming a cause on that evidence would have been a guess dressed as a finding, which is the failure mode this project treats as worse than an admitted unknown. (2) THE STRONG FINDING, and the half that IS provable: NO project code or deploy path can produce a soft-block. Exhaustive audit of src/ + scripts/ + deploy/: ZERO `rfkill block`, ZERO `nmcli radio off`, ZERO `hciconfig <dev> down`, ZERO `systemctl stop/disable/mask bluetooth`, ZERO `bluetoothctl power off`. Every radio verb the repo ships points the other way (pair_obdlink.sh:224 `power on`, pair_obdlink_driver.py:300 `_send("power on")`, deploy-pi.sh:838 + the unit `rfkill unblock all`); connect_obdlink.sh's `rfcomm release` is the closest thing to a teardown and it removes a KERNEL BINDING, not radio state. So the surviving explanation is an external/manual action that systemd-rfkill then saved at shutdown exactly as designed -- Atlas's hypothesis, corroborated (NOT proven) by commit ad59561 showing a live-Pi BT 'pairing-saga' debug session dated exactly 2026-07-03. Recorded as suggestive, not conclusive. (3) THE ONE THE PM MUST ACT ON -- AC2 offers a fork: document a prevention OR confirm the unblock service is sufficient mitigation. I could NOT confirm sufficiency, because auditing it turned up a REAL, LIVE-VERIFIED DEFECT. eclipse-rfkill-unblock.service ordered itself After=systemd-rfkill.service -- the PRODUCER half, which its own header calls 'the fix' -- and Before= NOTHING project-owned. Neither rfcomm-bind.service nor eclipse-obd.service declared any relationship to it, so systemd was free to start all three concurrently. Proven on the box, not inferred: `systemctl show` returns Before=multi-user.target shutdown.target only, and on the 2026-07-31 boot rfcomm-bind and eclipse-rfkill-unblock BOTH entered active at 20:25:59 -- the same second. Harmless that boot because the block had already been zeroed by hand; on the one boot where a block IS saved it is a coin flip, and the losing side binds /dev/rfcomm0 against a dark adapter while EVERY unit still reads `active` -- the exact 'green-looking unit on a dark adapter' the unit's header set out to prevent. WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT (sixth sighting this sprint of the US-494/499/502/503/505 two-correct-halves shape): the pre-existing test_unitManifest_ordersTheUnblockBeforeTheRfcommBind asserted the ordering against unit_manifest.START_ORDER, a hand-ordered PYTHON TUPLE. unit_manifest's own header states its ordering is 'grounded in the units' own declarations, NOT invented' and then lists the declarations it relies on -- none of which mention the unblock unit. So that was the single entry in the tuple with nothing behind it. The manifest is not decorative (obdctl sequences its own start/stop by it) but it CANNOT order boot, and boot is exactly when a restored block bites. FIX: Before=rfcomm-bind.service eclipse-obd.service. `Before=` and deliberately NOT `Wants=` -- it orders those consumers if they are already in the boot transaction and must never pull them in; no cycle (the unblock is After=bluetooth.service and neither consumer is an ancestor). NO deploy-script change needed: step_install_rfkill_unblock is cmp -s-guarded, so the changed unit installs + daemon-reloads on the next routine deploy -- BUT THE RACE IS STILL LIVE ON THE PI UNTIL THAT DEPLOY RUNS. PREVENTION SHIPPED: tests/deploy/test_no_radio_disable_in_project.py, a repo-wide static guard that turns finding (2) from a point-in-time audit into a standing invariant. US-512 already guards this at RUNTIME but only for two helpers and only for commands they emit -- a new script or deploy step is invisible to it. Guard design notes: patterns match ARGV LISTS as well as shell strings, because its own self-test caught on the FIRST run that a whitespace-only separator sees every `sudo rfkill block` and misses every `subprocess.run(["rfkill","block"])` -- which is the form bluetooth_helper actually uses; `\bblock\b` after a token separator so `rfkill unblock all` is not condemned (otherwise the guard flags the FIX for the outage it prevents -- pinned by an explicit permit-list test over all 8 restorative forms); whole-line # comments stripped per US-501's lesson, since bluetooth_helper.py and obd_connection.py both DOCUMENT these forbidden commands and a raw-text scanner would flag the prose explaining the rule; tests/ deliberately not scanned because US-512's guards assert on these strings literally; greppable `radio-guard-exempt` escape hatch per the explicit-hatch-over-drift rule. MUTATION-PROVED end-to-end, not just as regex: a real violating .sh dropped into scripts/ trips test_noShippedFileDisablesARadio with a precise file:line message (probe removed). The 4 new ordering tests were RED-first for the right reason before the unit changed. ONE DISCRIMINATOR DELIBERATELY LEFT UNTESTED, flagged to PM: whether `bluetoothctl power off` can itself produce a SAVED block. Settling it means disabling a radio on the car Pi and rebooting; I declined under the standing 'never disable a radio on the Pi remotely' rule (the 2026-07-19 nmcli radio wifi off stranding), with an owed engine-on drive on the box. Safe path is a bench Pi or the car Pi with the CIO present, and it changes NO conclusion above -- the project does not issue that command either way. ALSO FLAGGED TO PM (box-config, not mine to change): the Pi's ~1-week journal retention is the single reason this RCA cannot close harder; a SystemMaxUse=/MaxRetentionSec= bump would make the next slow-burn fault answerable. stories.completionNotes: THE conditionalOutcome RESOLVED FIRST, because it decides the size of the story: the pitch was NOT already gyro-fused, so this did not narrow to 'add ZUPT'. But the AC's phrasing understates the situation in the other direction too -- it was not raw accel-only either. US-478 low-passed the accel over 5 s (gravityTauSec) and read the pitch off that vector, which is why the defect never showed on a bench: a 1 s acceleration IS attenuated >90%. A 10 s on-ramp is 2 tau and propagates almost fully. So the phantom was real, just DELAYED, which is worse than obvious -- it appears only under exactly the sustained pull nobody reproduces at a desk. Worth stating precisely because 'accel-only' would have sent a reviewer looking for a bug that is not in the code. TWO FACTS THAT MADE THIS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS, both verified not assumed: raw.imu.gyro has been published by sensor_reader since US-410 (same burst, same seq) and the bridge simply never subscribed; and raw.obd.SPEED is published onto the SAME SampleBus by the capture loop (realtime._publishReading, gated by the same pi.bus.enabled that builds this bridge). So ZUPT needed NO new acquisition path and the bridge is still a pure bus consumer -- it opens no I2C device and no OBD connection, and cannot re-introduce the A-17 second-connection race. Two more subscription topics, nothing else. THE SIGN I DERIVED RATHER THAN GUESSED, and it is the one thing in here that silently breaks everything if wrong: the gyro-integrated pitch must agree with the accel tilt convention or the two halves of the filter fight each other and the estimate is worse than either alone. The frame is right-handed (forward x left = up), so a nose point moves as omega x forward = -omega_left * up: NOSE UP IS A NEGATIVE LEFT-AXIS RATE, pitchRate = -gyro[1]. Pinned by test_update_positiveLeftAxisRate_isNoseDown and mutation-proved (flipping it reds 3 tests including the ZUPT drift-correction one). Documented in the function so the next person does not re-derive it under pressure. Related caveat I chose to DOCUMENT rather than guard: an angular rate is a pseudovector, so resolveMountFrame is only correct for it if the mount map is a proper rotation (det +1). Every physically realizable remount is; a mirrored axis map is a config typo that already breaks the heading the same way. Adding a determinant check felt like scope. THE CONSTANT THAT DESERVES THE MOST SCRUTINY, and I have routed it to Spool with the arithmetic (AC4): accelTrustBand = 0.02. Specific force under a longitudinal a is sqrt(1+a^2), so a magnitude gate at band b admits a ~ sqrt(2b). At 0.02 that is ~0.2 g and the story's 0.3 g case (1.044 g, a 4.4% excess) is rejected outright -- pinned DIRECTLY by test_accelTrustBand_rejectsTheAccelerationItWasSizedFor, so AC5's guarantee is a property of the constant rather than an accident of the simulation. But I am not hiding the residual: magnitude is a WEAK discriminator at small a (sqrt(1+a^2) ~ 1 + a^2/2, so 0.1 g is only 0.5% off 1 g while contributing 5.7 deg of tilt error), and tightening much below ~0.5% would let road vibration gate the accel off permanently, leaving pure gyro drift with nothing to correct it. A sustained sub-0.2 g pull therefore still leaks in, bounded by the tau blend and erased at the next ZUPT -- which is precisely why Spool specified BOTH mechanisms and not either alone. pitchTauSec/accelTrustBand/zuptSpeedMaxAgeSec/zuptMinStops/zuptWindowStops are all Rex-derived, all config keys, all in the note to Spool. zuptMinStopSec is his [EXACT:3] and is 3.0, verbatim, with its own test asserting the constant. THE DANGEROUS NEGATIVE CASE IS NOT A FAILED SPEED READ, IT IS A STALE ONE -- same shape as US-518's route gate, and it is the single most valuable thing in this story. If the BT link drops while the car is stopped at a light (BL-025 is not hypothetical), the last thing the estimator ever heard is 'speed 0'. Honouring that would keep HARD-SNAPPING the attitude to whatever the accelerometer says for the rest of the drive -- i.e. pinning pitch to the 16.7-degree phantom on every on-ramp, with MORE confidence than the drift it was fixing. Guarded two ways: zuptSpeedMaxAgeSec (2.0, deliberately BELOW the 3 s gate) retires the stop, and confirmation requires zero speed OBSERVED ACROSS the window (lastSpeedCapture - stopSince > 3), not 3 s ELAPSED since one reading. That second rule matters on a slow/jittery SPEED poll, where wall-clock sampling would manufacture stops that never happened. AND AN ABSENT SPEED IS NEVER A ZERO SPEED: on a bench Pi with no OBD, no stop is ever confirmed and no bias is ever claimed. MUTATION TESTING EARNED ITS KEEP AND CAUGHT A BAD TEST OF MINE. 6 mutants: drop the near-1g gate -> 7 red incl. the real-chain end-to-end; drop the staleness guard -> 1 red; flip the gyro sign -> 3 red; bias from a single stop -> 1 red; gravity fallback for gradePct -> 2 red. The SIXTH -- confirm a stop on elapsed time instead of observed span -- SURVIVED on the first run, because my test was being saved by the freshness guard rather than by the rule it claimed to test. Fixed by widening zuptSpeedMaxAgeSec in that test so the guard cannot mask it, plus a new slow-poll test (two zero readings 2 s apart = 2 s of evidence + 1 s of hope, must NOT confirm). Both now kill it. Stated plainly because 'all mutants killed' would have been false on the first pass. HONEST-INSTRUMENT, per branch: pitch starts None and is never a fabricated 0.0 (new reason pitch_unseeded, deliberately DISTINCT from tilt_unresolved -- the sensor is fine, the attitude is simply not known yet, and gradePct null beats a confident 0.0 'flat road'); it seeds ONLY from an uncontaminated reading, because seeding mid-pull bakes the phantom in as the origin the gyro then integrates from; no bias until zuptMinStops stops, since a bias from one stop is the slope of a parking spot reported as a calibration constant; the bias window is ROLLING so a physical remount ages out instead of freezing on an old value; a stale gyro is not integrated (the US-478 frozen-compass rule, carried over); an unplug drops the attitude but KEEPS the bias (how the board is bolted in did not change when the cable did). ONE FACT, ONE PRODUCER: gradePct has NO gravity fallback. A fallback would have kept every existing test green while silently restoring the exact defect this story deletes -- mutation-proved, and it is why that test exists. The gravity low-pass is NOT gone: it still owns the g-meter level frame and the heading tilt-compensation, which are a different job (residual extraction, not attitude). Deliberately left alone -- re-pointing them was unrequested and would have changed a shipped card. SCOPE HELD: Spool's US-508 items 2 and 3 (gate the integrand at >=5 km/h and |dv/dt| < 0.15 g; slew-clamp |sin(pitch)| <= 0.15) are NOT here. They belong to the INTEGRAND, i.e. US-519, which is deferred pending his sigma. Flagged in his note as tracked-not-lost.
